OriginalP1issue: Potential overlapping/companion cohort; identical sham PCA/morphine values and near-identical active/control values.
Quantitativeaction: Exclude both publications from any common pooled model until overlap is adjudicated; keep one unresolved publication-family study unit.
CanStataproceed: YES — for all other studies; NO — for including either Yeh report
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Confirm whether cohorts overlap wholly/partly. If unresolved, retain both on duplicate-family hold.
Decisionrule: Exact identical sham PCA values + near-identical active/control data make independence unsafe.
Notes: v20/v22 primary opioid sheets already exclude both reports from independent pooling.

OriginalP1issue: Abstract medians/IQR differ from main Results/Figure 4.
Quantitativeaction: Use main Results/Figure 4 values: 0.70 (0.50–1.10) vs 0.90 (0.65–1.25) mg; retain abstract discrepancy as QC; sensitivity-only per AF lock.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Author correction desirable but not required for provisional sensitivity analysis.
Decisionrule: Main Results/Figure takes precedence over conflicting abstract summary.

OriginalP1issue: Same 3/43 vs8/43 counts have P=0.106 in Table 2 vs P=0.430 in prose.
Quantitativeaction: Use raw events 3/43 vs 8/43 to calculate RR/CI in Stata; do not use either published P value as the meta-analytic effect.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Correct publication P value is useful only for narrative reporting.
Decisionrule: Binary meta-analysis is calculated from events/denominators.

OriginalP1issue: Cumulative rescue count has P=0.004 in Table 3 vs0.04 in prose.
Quantitativeaction: Retain median/IQR rescue-administration counts 1 (1–3) vs 3.5 (2–7.8); do not infer effect from the conflicting P value. Pool only with a prespecified method suitable for non-normal count data.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Correct P value useful for narrative only.
Decisionrule: Native distribution data govern extraction; publication P discrepancy does not alter group values.

OriginalP1issue: 14/45 vs29/48; endpoint mixes PACU sufentanil and ward indomethacin; printed RR0.70 (0.44–1.10), P=0.005 is incompatible with raw counts.
Quantitativeaction: Exclude from opioid-specific rescue pooling. Retain 14/45 vs 29/48 only in mixed/undefined rescue evidence map; do not use printed RR/CI.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Separate PACU sufentanil and ward indomethacin counts would be needed to reclassify.
Decisionrule: Undefined mixed rescue endpoint cannot support an opioid-specific estimand.

OriginalP1issue: Rescue parecoxib table P=0.35 vs narrative P=0.58.
Quantitativeaction: For parecoxib rescue use raw counts 4/190 vs 7/188; calculate RR/CI directly. Ignore conflicting publication P=.35/.58 for quantitative synthesis.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Correct source P value optional for narrative.
Decisionrule: Binary effect comes from raw event counts.

OriginalP1issue: 48-h mean effective deliveries slightly exceed mean attempts in TEAS arm; exact MME totals only in unavailable supplement.
Quantitativeaction: Use verified 24-h PCA attempts/deliveries only. Exclude unresolved 48-h counter values and unavailable 48-h MME detail until supplement clarification.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: eTable 1 / corrected 48-h pump counters if a 48-h PCA analysis is later required.
Decisionrule: Outcome/timepoint-specific exclusion does not invalidate the verified 24-h result.

OriginalP1issue: Published 'up to postoperative48 h' total may include 30-min pre-end-of-surgery sufentanil; 2.25 vs2.5 μg/h infusion conflict.
Quantitativeaction: Keep total sufentanil only in broader/sensitivity 48-h analysis; exclude from strict postoperative-only 0–48-h primary model.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Author clarification required only to promote Xie into the strict Target-A pool.
Decisionrule: Published total may include 30-min pre-end-of-surgery opioid exposure.

OriginalP1issue: Exact opioid-consumption time window unclear; morphine-equivalent conversion differs between Methods and Table footnote.
Quantitativeaction: Exclude from fixed 24/48/72-h opioid pools. Retain binary opioid-use and author-defined MME only in evidence map/native-scale descriptive analyses.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Exact time window and actual conversion rule required for fixed-window MME synthesis.
Decisionrule: Unclear time window + inconsistent MME conversion prevents harmonized fixed-time pooling.

OriginalP1issue: 3.8(1.9) vs5.0(2.9) has no drug, unit, time window or interpretable metric.
Quantitativeaction: Exclude from quantitative synthesis; retain source text 3.8(1.9) vs 5.0(2.9) as unresolved descriptive result.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Drug, unit, metric, trigger, and time window required for re-entry.
Decisionrule: Undefined metric cannot be converted or classified safely.

OriginalP1issue: Printed intraoperative sufentanil 0.1 mg/kg per30 min appears implausible.
Quantitativeaction: Do not use the implausibly printed sufentanil dosing statement. The separately verified remifentanil result remains usable in its own sensitivity stratum.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Author correction only if intraoperative sufentanil itself is to be analyzed.
Decisionrule: One erroneous/unresolved source field does not invalidate a distinct source-supported remifentanil result.

OriginalP1issue: Cumulative rescue-dose count reported, but drug, dose and trigger unspecified.
Quantitativeaction: Retain rescue-dose-count result in mixed/undefined evidence map only; do not classify as opioid or non-opioid rescue.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Rescue drug, dose, route, trigger and prescriber/blinding required for reclassification.
Decisionrule: Drug identity is essential to an opioid-specific rescue estimand.

OriginalP1issue: Additional PCA-dose unit/drug/concentration not defined; POD2 anchored to first EA rather than surgery.
Quantitativeaction: Keep additional-PCA metric as descriptive native-scale result only; do not convert to opioid dose or assign to surgery-to-24-h pool.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: PCA drug/concentration/settings/unit and exact surgery-to-measurement interval.
Decisionrule: Undefined PCA physical unit prevents opioid-dose conversion.

OriginalP1issue: Total/effective PCIA use reported without exact cumulative time window.
Quantitativeaction: Retain PCIA-use counts in evidence map; do not assign to 24-h or 48-h PCA stratum.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Exact cumulative observation window and device-counter definitions.
Decisionrule: Time-window uncertainty blocks fixed-time pooling only.

OriginalP1issue: Rescue algorithm reported and significant, but exact group rescue quantities not given.
Quantitativeaction: Narrative/supportive rescue evidence only; no quantitative rescue effect because exact group rescue quantities are absent.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Group-level rescue tramadol/morphine counts or doses required for pooling.
Decisionrule: Statistical significance alone is not an extractable treatment effect.

OriginalP1issue: Exact 24-h mixed-PCIA volume is graph-only; text only gives4/8/36 h.
Quantitativeaction: Use exact text-reported 4-, 8-, and 36-h mixed-PCIA volumes only where relevant; exclude exact 24-h analysis unless a prespecified validated digitization is performed.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Exact 16/24-h numerical values or validated graph digitization for those timepoints.
Decisionrule: Do not invent graph-only point estimates.

OriginalP1issue: Reported total fentanyl means approach/exceed nominal reservoir implied by weight-based formulation.
Quantitativeaction: Retain source-reported 48-h fentanyl result in Target-A strict dataset, but require a leave-one-study-out/sensitivity model excluding An 2014 because of the reservoir plausibility concern.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Reservoir preparation/accounting clarification would remove the plausibility flag.
Decisionrule: Source value is reported and extractable; plausibility uncertainty is handled transparently by sensitivity analysis.

OriginalP1issue: Anesthesiologist masking and explicit remifentanil titration algorithm not reported; analyzed denominator smaller than randomized.
Quantitativeaction: Keep as intraoperative opioid exposure only; do not pool with clean protocol-titrated opioid-requirement studies.
Remainingsourceauthorneed: Anesthesiologist masking/titration algorithm needed only to promote into titrated-requirement stratum.
Decisionrule: Clinician-controlled exposure with incomplete titration reporting is a different estimand/quality stratum.

Studyresult: Wang Y et al. JAMA Surg 2023 (DOI 10.1001/jamasurg.2022.5674)

Quantitativeaction: Exclude from the review dataset and all meta-analyses. No numerical outcome row is required.
